Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the pre-operative image (Figure 1a), which shows a massive right-sided opacity causing leftward mediastinal shift, with the post-operative image (Figure 1c), there is clear evidence of surgical intervention (clips) and significant re-expansion of the right lung. However, the right hemidiaphragm remains elevated and some basal opacity persists, indicating only partial re-expansion, while the heart and trachea remain shifted to the left relative to a normal midline position due to residual volume loss or scarring.
